results.title: AI-driven non-destructive concrete stress state identification: A novel approach based on time–frequency analysis of active acoustic emission signals - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Full length article AI-driven non-destructive concrete stress state identification: A novel approach based on time–frequency analysis of active acoustic emission signals. Active AE technology collects waveform data of concrete under various stress states. Accurate and rapid identification of tunnel lining stress states is crucial for effective maintenance of tunnel structural safety. This paper presents an innovative method for intelligent non-destructive concrete stress state identification using time–frequency analysis of active acoustic emission (AE) wave signals. The approach combines advanced signal processing techniques with machine learning to achieve non-destructive assessment of concrete stress states in tunnel linings. The proposed method enables accurate classification and assessment of concrete stress states, strongly supporting the visualization of concrete state on active service and implementation of intelligent structural health monitoring. Based on the aforementioned challenges and research gaps, the primary objective of this study is to develop and validate a novel, AI-driven methodology for identifying concrete stress states by fully utilizing time–frequency domain information from active AE waveforms in conjunction with machine learning techniques.

results.title: Re-ACGAN: Structural damage identification with class-imbalance reweighted ACGAN for data augmentation - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Re-ACGAN: Structural damage identification with class-imbalance reweighted ACGAN for data augmentation. Jointly considering data augmentation (DA) and class-imbalance for vibration data. Data scarcity and class imbalance of vibration measurement pose a significant obstacle in data-driven structural damage identification. This study proposes an innovative class-imbalance reweighted auxiliary classifier generative adversarial network (Re-ACGAN) to augment vibration data aiming at advancing structural multiclass damage identification. The proposed Re-ACGAN incorporates two novel class-conditional reweighting mechanisms to adeptly address the class imbalance during data synthesis. Three diverse execution workflows for data augmentation (DA)-based damage classification are integrated to enhance damage identification performance. Numerical and experimental validations conducted on a well-known benchmark structure verify the improved precision of the proposed DA network in multiclass damage identification. Results indicate that after the introduction of the proposed class-imbalance reweighting modules, the synthetic data exhibit superior cluster structures and explicit class-conditional distribution patterns, providing intuitive evidence and explanations for understanding how the proposed reweighting mechanisms help enhance the data synthesis.
